subject: egg-shaped dwarf planet
title: What If You Stood on Haumea, the Dwarf Planet Shaped Like an Egg?

scenes.text: What if you stood on a world spinning so fast it stretched into an egg? Haumea does.
Haumea lies beyond Neptune, 43 times farther from the Sun than Earth. A day lasts 3.9 hours, the fastest spin of any large body out there.
The spin has flattened it into an egg about 2,300 kilometers long and 1,100 thick. The Sun is a bright star, rising again in under four hours.
Minus 240 degrees Celsius, under crystalline water ice. Two moons cross the sky. Overhead hangs a ring, 70 kilometers wide, found in 2017.
The ring circles once for every three spins. A year lasts 285 Earth years; nobody born here would see one through.
An egg world with its own ring, turning every four hours. Named after the Hawaiian goddess of childbirth.

description:
What if you stood on Haumea? This dwarf planet beyond Neptune spins once every 3.9 hours, faster than any other large body in the solar system, and the spin has stretched it into an ellipsoid roughly 2,300 by 1,700 by 1,100 kilometers.
Its surface is crystalline water ice at about minus 240 degrees Celsius, it has two moons, Hiiaka and Namaka, and a 2017 stellar occultation revealed a ring about 70 kilometers wide roughly 1,000 kilometers above the surface, in a 3 to 1 resonance with the spin. Haumea takes about 285 years to orbit the Sun.
